title: Travelling with a coach on a ClayAway tour
summary: ClayAway is a ClayArena service in preparation. A coach or organiser will gather a group, and each shooter will buy one package of training, accommodation, transfers and a shared programme.

body.html: Planning a trip yourself is interesting, but it takes effort. ClayArena is preparing another way: ClayAway tours with a coach. A coach or an organiser will gather a group of shooters, and each participant will buy one package.

The package is planned to include training at one or more shooting grounds, accommodation, transfers and a shared programme, such as dinners or excursions. If the group needs one, an interpreter who knows shooting terms will join.

What is included will depend on the tour, so read the description before booking. Are flights, targets, cartridges and gun hire in the package? Each tour will also say what it is mainly about — mostly training or mostly travel — and how many targets you will shoot per day.

The main advantage will be a coach beside you each day. A coach who knows the grounds can help with technique for Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting and with the targets you will meet there. A group with the same hobby also makes the trip more fun.

Times in a tour programme will be given in the venue's time zone, with the zone labelled. After the flight, check that your phone shows local time. Long flights east call for a spare day: see Jet lag and the first days at a new ground.

Gun documents stay the responsibility of each shooter. The tour organiser will be able to help with an invitation letter and advice on local rules, but the permits are applied for by the gun's owner. If taking a gun is difficult, ask whether one can be hired at the destination. More in Travelling with a gun inside the EU and Outside the EU: national permits.

If a tour includes a competition under FITASC rules, nobody may coach a competitor during it (Chapter 8 · No coaching during competition, Chapter 21 · No coaching during competition). The coach works with you before and after, and on the stand you shoot on your own. An interpreter then passes on only official information, so that it is not taken for coaching. Other events can have their own rules: read the programme.

For organisers: the organiser and the coach do not have to be the same person. The organiser may be the coach, but also a manager, a club, a shooting ground or an agency. It is the organiser who will be responsible for the tour.

Each tour will have its own name: the coach or the place, plus the format, for example “Cyprus Shooting & Food Week”. In the catalogue and on its card, the tour will carry the label “ClayAway”. The organiser will choose the coach, the grounds, the dates, the group size and the disciplines.

Plan the hotel, the transfers to the grounds and the shared programme together. If participants speak different languages, invite an interpreter who knows shooting terms. Give the timetable in the venue's time zone, with the zone labelled.

Remember the law. Rules for carrying guns and cartridges differ between countries, and participants may need, for example, the European Firearms Pass or an invitation letter. Help the group with documents early, but each shooter must make sure their own papers are in order.

Each person on a tour will have a role, such as organiser, coach, participant or companion, and will see the information that role needs. Booking and payment details will be published when ClayAway launches.
A good tour is one after which the participants shoot better and want to come again. So describe the programme, the price and the level the tour is aimed at honestly.

key_points.html: ClayAway (in preparation): a coach or organiser will gather a group, and the shooter will buy one package.
Before booking, check what the package includes and what the tour is mainly about.
Programme times will be in the venue's time zone, with the zone labelled.
Gun documents stay the owner's responsibility.
At a FITASC competition, no coaching: the coach works with you before and after.

quiz.q: What will a shooter buy on a ClayAway tour?

options.text: Only the flight to the venue
One package: training, stay, transfers, programme
Only the targets and the cartridges

quiz.explain: ClayAway is planned to bundle the main parts of the trip into one package.

quiz.q: Who will be able to organise a ClayAway tour?

options.text: A coach, manager, club, ground or agency
Only the coach who leads the training
Only FITASC or a national federation

quiz.explain: Organiser and coach are different roles, although a coach can organise a tour too.

quiz.q: At a FITASC competition, may the tour coach give you tips on the stand?

options.text: Yes, because it is part of the package
Yes, if the referee does not object
No, coaching during the competition is not allowed

quiz.explain: Under the FITASC rules the coach works with you before and after the competition, but not during it.

sources.title: FITASC — official rules of Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting
